conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: Compile-Time Arithmetic (Mode of arithmetic used and rules for intermediate data handling)
rows.adjudicator-notes: Row written from CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator: EvalArith rides System.Decimal (+,-,*,/ with OverflowException -> CtDiagCode.ArithmeticRule; '/' by zero rejected), EvaluateArithmeticOperand applies decimal.Truncate to an expression's final result. Probes /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s1/probe/i29.cob (--std 2002 and 2023): C1 2/3*3=2, C2 100/7*7=100, C3 1/3*3=0, C4 (2.5e-28 tie) =2, C5 (7.5e-28 tie) =8 -> round-half-even, C6 -7/2=-3, C7 exact product 11111111111110888888888888, C8 2.5+0=2; i29b.cob overflow -> COBOLNET1547; i29c.cob >>DEFINE X AS 7 / 2 * 2 -> 7 (same evaluator). ⚠ docs/CONFORMANCE.md §3 bullet 'Compile-time arithmetic mode' (line 504) contradicts this row ('standard fixed-point decimal mode', 'division truncates', multiplication exact) — kb/Work PB1369 (open) owns that bullet; the integrator should replace it with a pointer to this row in the same change set. cite.py --check 7.3.6.3 'The implementor shall define and document which mode of arithmetic ...' OK (2); 7.3.6.2 'They shall also document which intermediate rounding method is used' OK (2); 7.3.6.3 'The final result ... truncated to the integer part' OK (3). rows.subject: Compiler directives
rows.adjudicator-notes: §7.3.3 SR9 'The compiler-directive word 'IMP' is reserved for use by the implementor. If the implementor defines the IMP directive, the syntax rules for that directive shall be implementor-defined.' (cite.py --check 7.3.3 OK). COBOL.NET defines NO IMP directive: no constructs.json row claims 'IMP' as a directiveWord, so >>IMP is an unrecognized word left for the parser - I1 '>>IMP SOMETHING' and I3 '>> IMP' are rejected (COBOL0001). The conditional second sentence is therefore vacuous, and Annex A.1 item 30 (IMP syntax/general rules) is conditionally required only 'upon support for an IMP directive', so no CONFORMANCE.md entry is owed. CompilerDirectiveCatalogDriftTests.Roster_Matches_TheSpecSection keeps any non-standard directive word from entering the catalog without a clause (a drift test, not a spec-derived closer). The use of IMP as a compilation-variable-name (I2 '>>DEFINE IMP AS 1' accepted) is the §7.3.11.3 SR1 / SR-7.3.3-7 reservation defect, charged there. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the >> compiler-directive facility is absent from X3.23-1985; per-directive introducing editions are the §7.3.x rows' own, e.g. PUSH/POP added in 2023 per Annex E.3.3 item 38 and E.2 item 5)
rows.rule-text: The compiler-directive word 'IMP' is reserved for use by the implementor. If the implementor defines the IMP directive, the syntax rules for that directive shall be implementor-defined. NOTE >>IMP provides an optional place holder for all current and future implementor-defined directives. In this way the implementor can optionally support the use of >>IMP to indicate the start of one or more implementor-defined directives.

rows.subject: Compiler directives
rows.adjudicator-notes: §7.3.4 GR4 'If the implementor defines the IMP directive, the general rules for that directive shall be implementor-defined.' (cite.py --check 7.3.4 OK). Conditional on an implementor IMP directive, which COBOL.NET does not define (no catalog row claims IMP; I1/I3 '>>IMP ...' rejected). The rule is vacuous for this implementation and Annex A.1 item 30 is owed only 'upon support for an IMP directive'. Nothing to test beyond SR-7.3.3-9's rejection. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the >> compiler-directive facility is absent from X3.23-1985; per-directive introducing editions are the §7.3.x rows' own, e.g. PUSH/POP added in 2023 per Annex E.3.3 item 38 and E.2 item 5)
rows.rule-text: If the implementor defines the IMP directive, the general rules for that directive shall be implementor-defined.

rows.subject: Computer independent data description
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'The non-combining character and the following combining characters of a composite sequence defined in ISO/IEC 10646 are each treated as a single character position.' (cite.py --check 8.5.1.4 -> OK §8.5.1.4 1)). The typed-native substrate stores alphanumeric and national text as .NET UTF-16 code units, one char per character position (D-N1; CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-188), with no grapheme/StringInfo/normalization anywhere on the character-position path (searched src for StringInfo/TextElement/EnumerateRunes/Normalize: only the ISO 14651 collation engine and CLDR builder walk codepoints, which is the STANDARD-COMPARE algorithm, not character-position processing). PROBE (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023, out/probe/cidd/p1.cob): N"e"+U+0301 -> FUNCTION LENGTH = 2; PIC N(3) VALUE that literal: (1:1) = N"e", (2:1) = NX"0301"; INSPECT TALLYING FOR CHARACTERS BEFORE N" " = 02. All as the rule requires (base and mark each one position). No spec-derived golden pins a combining sequence (grep of tests/conformance for 0301/combining: none) -> test-ref empty. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the ISO/IEC 10646 / UTF-16 national facility enters with ISO 1989:2002; the 2023 Annex E lists no change to 8.5.1.4; X3.23-1985 has no ISO/IEC 10646 coded character set, so the rule is vacuous at 85)
rows.rule-text: The non-combining character and the following combining characters of a composite sequence defined in ISO/IEC 10646 are each treated as a single character position.

rows.subject: Computer independent data description
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'The high-half 2 octets and the low-half 2 octets of a four-octet sequence defined in the UTF-16 format of ISO/IEC 10646 are each treated as a single character position.' and the NOTE: 'Each two-octet code element of UTF-16 is treated in COBOL as though it were itself a character' (cite.py --check 8.5.1.4 -> OK §8.5.1.4 2) for both). Code: one .NET char per character position; REVERSE is Array.Reverse over chars (splits the pair, as the rule requires); NationalCollation native order = code-unit order. PROBES (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/cidd/p1.cob, p2.cob, p3.cob) with U+1F600 = D83D DE00: FUNCTION LENGTH(N"<U+1F600>") = 2 and LENGTH("<U+1F600>") = 2 (alphanumeric repertoire is UTF-16 too); PIC N(4) VALUE N"a<U+1F600>b": (2:1)=NX"D83D", (3:1)=NX"DE00", (4:1)=N"b"; INSPECT FOR CHARACTERS = 04; MOVE N"<U+1F600>" TO PIC N(1) truncates to NX"D83D" (the lone high half); REVERSE puts DE00 at position 2; PIC N(2) round-trips the pair; PIC N(1) VALUE N"<U+1F600>" is refused COBOLNET0898 (§13.18.63.3 SR5 — cite.py OK — the literal is 2 positions); a record NX"D83D0041D83D" with lone high halves round-trips byte-exactly through SEQUENTIAL and LINE SEQUENTIAL files (d8 3d 00 41 d8 3d) and BYTE-LENGTH = 6. Both halves (high and low) verified. Existing goldens cite 8.5.1.4 (2002/l1_char_national_argument_bound, 2002/l1_char_national_also_positions, 85/pb190_reverse_argument_shapes) but none places a surrogate code unit in data, so none is a covering test -> test-ref empty. Adjacent, not this rule: UPPER-CASE/LOWER-CASE use ToUpperInvariant, which maps a supplementary pair (e.g. U+10428->U+10400) as one character; the spec's own Annex C.2 case table lists supplementary mappings (10400,10428), so that is a §15.97/C.2 question for those rows, not a §8.5.1.4 defect. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the ISO/IEC 10646 / UTF-16 national facility enters with ISO 1989:2002; the 2023 Annex E lists no change to 8.5.1.4; X3.23-1985 has no ISO/IEC 10646 coded character set, so the rule is vacuous at 85)
rows.rule-text: The high-half 2 octets and the low-half 2 octets of a four-octet sequence defined in the UTF-16 format of ISO/IEC 10646 are each treated as a single character position. NOTE The UTF-16 format of ISO/IEC 10646 is a coded character set where each code element (or 'code value') consists of two octets. Many, but not all, of the letters and symbols are represented in one code element. In order to accommodate more entities than could otherwise be defined in a two-octet coded character set, the following techniques are used in ISO/IEC 10646: — some abstract characters or text entities are defined as 'combining character sequences' of multiple code elements where a two-octet base character and one or more two-octet combining characters form a complete entity, together called a composite sequence. — some abstract characters or text entities are defined as 'surrogate pairs' consisting of two code elements. These techniques facilitate efficient processing of data as fixed-size two-octet code elements, but present opportunities for corruption of data if not handled correctly. To achieve a better understanding, see ISO/IEC 10646. COBOL does not provide any special handling or recognition of surrogate pairs; nor does COBOL provide recognition of composite sequences. Each two-octet code element of UTF-16 is treated in COBOL as though it were itself a character. Users are responsible for ensuring that any truncation, replacement, or reference-modification that occurs is consistent with the needs of their application.

Probes at --std 2023 (IMPLEMENTS RETURNING): prototype X ONLY / implementation X ONLY accepted (R5F1); implementation X without ONLY refused 0841 (R5F2); implementation Y ONLY where Y INHERITS X refused (R5F3 â€” ONLY forbids the subclass). MethodConformanceMismatches: (m1.Binding.Returning is null) != (m2.Binding.Returning is null) -> 'RETURNING presence differs from ... (ISO Â§9.3.8.2.3 rule 4)'. Both directions probed at --std 2023: R4A (prototype RETURNING R, implementation none) and R4B (prototype none, implementation RETURNING R) -> COBOLNET0841 'RETURNING presence differs from the IR4x prototype (ISO Â§9.3.8.2.3 rule 4)'. The same function serves overrides (ValidateOverrideSignatures, 0829) and InterfaceConformsTo, so every asker gets it. rows.subject: Conformance for object orientation
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule text (cite.py --check 9.3.8.2.3 OK: '7) If either of the corresponding formal parameters or returning items in interface-1 or interface-2 is a strongly-typed group item, both are of the same type.'). Code: DescriptionMismatch calls StrongTypeMismatch FIRST for every formal and for a non-object RETURNING; 'same type' is StrongTypeModel.SameType, i.e. Â§8.5.3.1 equivalence (cite.py --check 8.5.3.1 OK: 'Two type declarations are considered equivalent when they have the same type-name, both have the same presence or absence of the EXTERNAL clause and the STRONG phrase, and for each elementary item ...'). PB1012's adjudication question answered by measurement and text: an interface prototype CAN carry a strong type â€” Â§10.6.2 SR4 e) (cite OK) limits a prototype's data division to a linkage section, and a TYPEDEF entry is legal there (only Â§13.18.x level-1 / data-name constraints apply); 'the same type' across two source elements is Â§8.5.3.1 equivalence (same type-name, same STRONG/EXTERNAL, same elementary layout), which is what SameType implements. Probes at --std 2023 (TYPEDEF STRONG in each method's LINKAGE SECTION): identical TT declarations on both sides accepted and run (R7E); TT with F PIC X(5) vs X(4) refused (R7F); strong TT vs a plain group of the same width refused (R7G); RETURNING TT X(4) vs X(5) refused (R7H); TT vs TU identical layout refused (R7I, different type-name); TT STRONG vs TT non-strong refused (R7J). The WORKING-STORAGE route (R7A-D) is refused by Â§10.6.2 SR4 e) (2272), correctly. Both halves (formal and returning) verified. No spec-derived test covers rule 7 at the interface boundary -> test-ref empty. Recommend PB1012 record the adjudication (prototype LINKAGE TYPEDEF + Â§8.5.3.1). || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (strongly-typed groups: TYPEDEF STRONG, 2002+)
rows.rule-text: If either of the corresponding formal parameters or returning items in interface-1 or interface-2 is a strongly-typed group item, both are of the same type.

rows.subject: Constant conditional expression
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: arithmetic expression in a cce formed per §7.3.6 (cite.py --check 7.3.8.2 OK); §7.3.6.2 SR1a no exponentiation, SR1b fixed-point literal operands, SR1c no division by zero; §7.3.6.3 GR3 truncation to integer (--check 7.3.6.2 / 7.3.6.3 OK). Probes in >>IF (2023): c9 '2 ** 2 = 4' rejected SR1a; c15 '1 / 0 = 1' rejected SR1c; e2 '1.5E1 = 15' rejected (float, §7.3.3 SR10); c8 '7 / 2 = 3' TRUE and e1 '1.5 + 0 = 1' TRUE (GR3 truncation); d1 '1.5 = 1' FALSE (a sole literal is a literal operand, not truncated); c22 '1 + 2 > 2' TRUE; c21 ZERO rejected. No cce-context test pins all three SR1 halves (Cce_TrueFalse covers only truncation; the Rejects_* tests drive the operand evaluator outside a cce), so test-ref left empty.
rows.rule-text: An arithmetic expression in a constant conditional expression shall be formed in accordance with 7.3.6, Compile-time arithmetic expressions.

rows.subject: Constant conditional expression
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: boolean expression in a cce formed per §7.3.7 — operands boolean literals only (cite.py --check 7.3.8.2 and 7.3.7.2 OK). Probes (2023): f1 'B"1" B-AND "1" = B"1"' rejected (§7.3.7.2 SR1); f2 'B"1" B-AND 1' rejected; f4 undefined name X rejected; e6 'B"1" B-XOR B"1" = B"0"' TRUE; d9 'B"1" = B"1" B-AND B"0"' FALSE; f3 'B-NOT B"0"' TRUE. Operator semantics pinned by unit:CompileTimeBooleanCceTests.Boolean_BinaryAndUnary (operand evaluator, not cce context) — no cce-context formation-rejection test, so test-ref empty.
rows.rule-text: A boolean expression in a constant conditional expression shall be formed in accordance with 7.3.7, Compile-time boolean expressions.

rows.subject: Constant entry
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR4 (cite OK: "it is evaluated in accordance with 7.3.6") with §7.3.6.3 GR3 (cite OK: "The final result ... shall be truncated to the integer part of the value"). Probes: AS 7 / 2 -> 3; AS -7 / 2 -> -3 (INTEGER-PART toward zero); AS (0.5) -> 0 (parenthesized, not a single literal); AS 0.5 + 0.6 -> 1; AS 1 + 2 * 3 -> 7; golden K-EXPR (2+3)*4-6/2 = 17, K-TWICE = 10. Category numeric, integer (IsInteger true -> legal OCCURS/PIC repetition). Intermediate precision = .NET decimal, documented (CONFORMANCE.md line 515, §7.3.6.2 SR2). The accepted figurative ZERO operand is an SR6/SR7 defect, not an evaluation defect (F-ZERO-OPERAND). || REFUTED: CONFORMS (test-ref empty: conformance:2002/constant_entry does not pin the GR4 truncation/integer half) — The code conforms on every probe, but the cited golden does not pin the branch that makes GR4 distinct. Its only arithmetic-expression constants are K-EXPR = (2+3)*4-6/2 = 17 and K-TWICE = 10. Both are exact integers, so the §7.3.6.3 GR3 truncation never runs. Neither is used where only an integer may appear (the OCCURS bound and PIC repetition in the golden use the literal constants K-MAX and K-WID). So the 'Constant-name-1 is an integer' half is also unpinned. The golden verifies precedence and numeric category only. || Editions (adjudicator): 2002+/2014/2023: §13.10 is unchanged 2014->2023 (Annex E lists no constant-entry change); the 2002 introduction and which AS legs 2002 carried are not derivable from the 2023 text (dossier gap)
rows.rule-text: If arithmetic-expression-1 is specified, it is evaluated in accordance with 7.3.6, Compile-time arithmetic expressions, to determine the value of constant-name-1. The class and category of constant-name-1 is numeric. Constant-name-1 is an integer.
